c.tagline: Transylvania's youthful tech-and-student capital, from Gothic spires to the Untold festival.

taxi.fareNote: Licensed taxis are cheap and metered with the per-km rate posted on the door; Uber and Bolt are widely used, reliable, and often the easiest way to get around.

emergency.note: 112 covers police, fire, and ambulance nationwide; English-speaking operators are usually available.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Use ride-hailing apps or metered taxis to avoid overcharging, and keep usual awareness in the busy nightlife streets around Piața Unirii late at night.

hood_desc: The walkable historic heart around Unirii Square, dominated by the Gothic St. Michael's Church and the Matthias Corvinus statue, with the museum square (Piata Muzeului), cafes, and most of the nightlife; the obvious first-timer base.

A leafy, sought-after residential district west of the centre along the Somes River, near Central Park and the botanical gardens; calm and green, popular with families and academics, a short walk or ride from downtown.

A dense, lively mixed district north-east of the centre built around Piata Marasti and the huge Iulius Mall, with shops, restaurants, and good transit links; convenient and local rather than touristy.
A modern, fast-growing quarter of new apartments and tech offices near the eastern park and lakes; quiet and comfortable, favoured by the city's students and young professionals.

Cluj's largest neighbourhood, a sprawling, student-heavy residential district south-west of the centre with the medieval Calvaria church and Cetatuia hill views nearby; budget-friendly and authentically local.
lodging: DoubleTree by Hilton Cluj City Plaza

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink, though some locals prefer bottled for taste.

transit.hours: Buses, trolleybuses, and trams run roughly 5:00 AM to 11:00 PM, with a limited number of night lines on the main corridors.
transit.note: CTP runs the city's buses, trolleybuses, and a couple of tram lines; the compact centre around Unirii Square is easily walked, and Uber and Bolt fill late-night gaps cheaply.
transit.pay: Tap a contactless bank card directly on the validator, buy tickets from CTP kiosks or ticket machines, or use the 24pay app; a single ride is about 3 lei. Validate on boarding and keep proof for inspections.

bus: Autogara Beta / FANY & FlixBus intercity coaches

transit.m: CTP bus line 5 to the city centre (~30-40 min)

tip.r: Rounding up or leaving about 10% for good service at restaurants is appreciated but not obligatory; not customary for taxis.

food.name: Varza a la Cluj
food.desc: The city's own dish - layers of sour cabbage, minced pork and rice baked in a clay pot and finished with smoked bacon and a spoon of sour cream.

places.name: Varzarie
places.note: A restaurant built around cabbage dishes; the obvious place to eat the city's namesake casserole.

places.name: Roata
places.note: The traditional Transylvanian house locals send visitors to; generous portions, book at weekends.

places.name: Casa Maramureseana
places.note: Maramures regional cooking in the old town, strong on baked cabbage and pork dishes.

food.name: Mici
food.desc: Skinless grilled rolls of beef, lamb and pork spiced with garlic and pepper, eaten with mustard, white bread and a cold beer.

places.name: Piata Mihai Viteazul market
places.note: Grill stalls around the big central market cook mici to order for market shoppers.

places.name: Roata
places.note: Charcoal grill plates of mici and pork with pickles; the classic Cluj garden-terrace meal.

places.name: Casa Maramureseana
places.note: Traditional grill selection in the centre, handy if you want mici with table service.

food.name: Ciorba (sour soup)
food.desc: Soured with bors or lemon - radauteana with chicken and garlic cream, burta with tripe, or peasant vegetable ciorba, always with hot chilli and sour cream.

places.name: Zama
places.note: Soup-focused Romanian kitchen; several ciorba varieties served daily in bread bowls or pots.

places.name: Roata
places.note: Reliable rotating ciorba list to start a full Transylvanian meal.

places.name: Casa Maramureseana
places.note: Well reviewed soups and regional starters in a wood-and-textile village-style room.

food.name: Sarmale cu mamaliga
food.desc: Minced pork and rice rolled in soured cabbage or vine leaves, slow-cooked with smoked meat and served on polenta with sour cream.

places.name: Casa Maramureseana
places.note: Maramures-style sarmale with smoked pork, one of the dishes reviewers mention most.

places.name: Roata
places.note: Homestyle sarmale and polenta at fair prices; the standard Cluj introduction to Romanian food.

places.name: Varzarie
places.note: Cabbage specialist, so sarmale are a house speciality rather than an afterthought.

food.name: Papanasi
food.desc: Warm fried doughnut rings of sweet cheese dough, topped with a doughnut ball, thick sour cream and sour cherry jam - one order feeds two.

places.name: Roata
places.note: Widely called the best papanasi in Cluj; order one between two people.

places.name: Casa Maramureseana
places.note: Traditional fried version with smantana and visinata jam in the old town.

places.name: Varzarie
places.note: Rounds off the savoury Transylvanian menu with the classic cheese-dough dessert.

food.name: Kurtoskalacs
food.desc: Hungarian chimney cake - sweet dough wound round a spit, rolled in sugar and roasted over coals until caramelised, then coated in walnut or cinnamon.

places.name: Piata Unirii stalls
places.note: Chimney-cake spits turn on the main square daily and all through the Christmas market.

places.name: Piata Muzeului stalls
places.note: Kiosks around the museum square bake kurtoskalacs fresh for the evening bar crowd.

places.name: Piata Mihai Viteazul market
places.note: Market bakers sell chimney cake and Hungarian pastries alongside the produce stalls.

food.name: Tuica and palinca
food.desc: Transylvanian fruit brandy - plum tuica or the stronger double-distilled palinca, drunk cold as a shot before the food arrives.

places.name: Roata
places.note: House palinca poured as the traditional opener to a long Transylvanian dinner.

places.name: Casa Maramureseana
places.note: Maramures horinca and palinca selection matching its regional food menu.

places.name: Varzarie
places.note: Keeps a short list of Romanian fruit brandies to go with the cabbage dishes.

food.name: Transylvanian wine
food.desc: Crisp whites from Jidvei, Lechinta and the Tarnave hills - feteasca regala, feteasca alba and muscat ottonel grown just south of the city.

places.name: Bricks M.A.R.e
places.note: Riverside fine dining with the city's most serious Romanian wine list.

places.name: Baracca
places.note: Long-running upmarket restaurant pairing modern Romanian plates with local bottles.

places.name: Bulgakov Cafe
places.note: Old-town cafe and bar institution, easy place to try Romanian wines by the glass.

landmarks: St. Michael's Church
One of Transylvania's mightiest Gothic churches has anchored Piața Unirii since the 14th century, its 80-meter neo-Gothic tower ruling the city skyline.
Piața Unirii (Union Square) and Matthias Corvinus Monument
Cluj's grand baroque-fronted main square centers on the sweeping equestrian monument to Hungarian king Matthias Corvinus, the city's most famous son.
Alexandru Borza Botanical Garden
Among southeastern Europe's finest botanical gardens, its 14 hectares fold in a Japanese garden, Roman garden, palm houses, and a panoramic water tower.
Bánffy Palace (National Museum of Art)
Transylvania's most beautiful baroque palace, an 18th-century aristocratic residence, now hangs Romanian masters around its statue-crowned courtyard facade.
Cetățuia Hill
The wooded hill of an 18th-century Habsburg fortress rises just across the Someș River, offering Cluj's best sunset panorama over spires and rooftops.
Dormition of the Theotokos Orthodox Cathedral
This monumental interwar cathedral in Brâncovenesc style dominates Avram Iancu Square, its great dome a proud statement of Romanian Orthodox identity.
Matthias Corvinus House
The 15th-century Gothic merchant house where the great Renaissance king was born in 1443 is Cluj's oldest preserved dwelling.
Museum Square and the Franciscan Church
Cluj's oldest square charms with the medieval Franciscan monastery church, the Carolina Obelisk, and the liveliest cafe terraces in the historic center.
Central Park (Parcul Central Simion Bărnuțiu) and the Casino
A 19th-century chestnut-lined park along the Someș with a rowing lake and the elegantly restored Casino pavilion, now a cultural center.
Tailors' Bastion (Bastionul Croitorilor)
A 15th-century defensive tower at the old citadel's southeast corner, restored into a cultural centre for exhibitions after guarding Cluj's city walls for over four centuries.

train.note: Cluj-Napoca's station sits on the main Transylvanian line, with CFR Calatori trains to Bucharest (~8-9h via Brasov), Oradea, Timisoara, Sighisoara, and Brasov, plus a daytime international service west to Budapest via Oradea. Trains are slow and scenic - many travellers prefer the bus or a domestic flight for longer hops.

bus.note: Long-distance coaches (FlixBus and Romanian operators such as FANY and Normandia) leave from the city's autogari, serving Budapest, Vienna, and cities across Western Europe where Romania's large diaspora lives, plus domestic routes to Bucharest, Brasov, and Timisoara.

ferry.note: Cluj-Napoca sits inland in Transylvania on the shallow Someșul Mic river, hundreds of kilometres from the sea, so no passenger ferry or river boat services exist.

full.blurb: A magnificent star-shaped Vauban citadel and Romania's symbolic 'coronation' city, about 1h30 south.
full.name: Alba Iulia

full.blurb: A UNESCO-listed medieval walled citadel, one of Europe's best-preserved and the birthplace of Vlad the Impaler, about 2h30 by road.
full.name: Sighisoara

full.blurb: Karst caves, gorges, and traditional villages in the Apuseni Natural Park west of the city, including the famous Pestera Ursilor (Bear's Cave).
full.name: Apuseni Mountains & Bear's Cave

half.blurb: A vast underground salt mine turned surreal subterranean park with an amphitheatre, Ferris wheel, and boating lake, about 30 min south.
half.name: Salina Turda (Turda Salt Mine)

half.blurb: A dramatic limestone gorge with cliff-side hiking trails and rare wildlife, near Turda about 40 min from the city.
half.name: Cheile Turzii (Turda Gorge)

half.blurb: The 'world's most haunted forest' on the city's western edge, with twisted trees, walking trails, and a paragliding meadow.
half.name: Hoia-Baciu Forest
